internal.title: Incident Resolved: High Kafka Consumer Lag in Accounting Service
internal.body:
At 11:47 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert for high Kafka consumer lag was triggered in the accounting service. Initial diagnosis identified an error injection related to the kafkaQueueProblems feature flag as the root cause. This flag was recently enabled and coincided with increased error ratios and latency in the service.

At 12:06 UTC, the decision was made to disable the kafkaQueueProblems flag. This action was approved and executed promptly. Following the flag disablement, monitoring confirmed recovery with normalized error ratios and latency metrics.

The incident was resolved without further impact to service availability or customer transactions.

Timeline:
- 11:47 UTC: Alert received for KafkaConsumerLagHigh
- 12:06 UTC: Diagnosis identified error injection from kafkaQueueProblems flag
- 12:06 UTC: Flag disablement proposed, approved, and executed
- 12:06 UTC: Recovery verified with normalized metrics

Please review the postmortem for detailed analysis and lessons learned.

external.body: Between 11:47 and 12:07 UTC on 2026-11-08, the accounting service experienced processing delays due to an internal configuration issue affecting message consumption. This caused temporary delays in transaction processing. The issue was identified and resolved promptly, and normal service operation has resumed. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your understanding.
